steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: What's the score?

steps.name: Sweating Worker
steps.text: You're ahead by ten. How about you just let me have this one?

steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: I'll let ya have shit... watch this—strike from behind the back!
Big Tooth—Big Tooth! My throat's smoldering!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Pour me a pint! A big one! Quick!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And a bottle of carrot soda!

steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: A-Alanna?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You dropped your toothpick, Big Tooth—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Eww, don't put it back in your mouth! That's disgusting!

steps.name: Sweating Worker
steps.text: I-It's really her!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What's with that look like you just saw a ghost?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: It's been a while. A whole year since you kicked that door in.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Really? That long? Give me that beer on the bar. I'm dying of thirst.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Ah—

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: You said you came back for a violation ticket?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, got an electronic ticket from the Rim Billiton Big Pillar Autonomous Prefecture Residential Management Council while I was working overtime at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Residential Management Council? When did that happen... never mind. Keep going.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The ticket said I had a 'non-compliant building' under my name, and it'd be torn down if I didn't pay the fine before the deadline!

steps.name: Workers
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I know, right? I thought my old home was long gone!

steps.name: Sweating Worker
steps.text: We're surprised alright, but the most surprising thing is...

steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: You eat and sleep on your truck, can't walk straight on solid ground, and even made a bet that you can go without leaving your truck an entire year except to go to the bathroom...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: ...But you have a house? How?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It was my mum and dad's. Well, I guess I inherited it, but I thought it'd collapsed ages ago. Even if it didn't, no way it's habitable after a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: But now you got a ticket...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So I came back in a hurry. What if the people who organized the evacuation were wrong? What if the Catastrophe didn't come at all?

steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: If it's that important, why'd you come here first?

spans.text: If it's that important, why'd you come

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That might just be the smartest question to ever come out of your mouth, Big Tooth. Think about it. I gotta at least have a car if I'm gonna try to find the place after all these years, right?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Ah, gotcha. But you don't just want a car, you want someone to drive it for you, don't ya?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Of course. I never drive tired. Sounds like you're interested?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Alanna of the Barrenlands, the free spirit who drifts like the wind, has a secret den of her own? Of course I'm interested!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Deal! Righto, no time like the present. Let's get moving—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Grab a few bottles of carrot soda from Big Tooth over there. No need to pay—he owes me. And make sure they're cold!

steps.name: Worker Biting Toothpick
steps.text: Heh, take as many as ya like. All good, girlie. Good health to ya.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Th-Thank you...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: It's not on this map either?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Maybe the maps are too new... How could a big town like that just vanish from the map? It's only been a decade or so.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Well, we can't keep driving in circles. Anything else about the town that stands out, besides the Catastrophe?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Lemme think. There was a mine next to it, and the townsfolk all worked there.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: That describes like 99% of the towns in Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Were your mum and dad miners too, Lanns?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Well, not exactly. They worked at the mines, though. Mum was an accountant, and pops was a welder. Why?

spans.text: the mines, though. Mum was an accountant, and pops was a welder. Why?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Nothing, just that you've never talked about them before.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Wait... I think I remember this intersection!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Try taking a right.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, this is it! Keep going!

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Judging by the road signs, this road's been worked on recently.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Maybe someone's still living here!
Alanna pokes her head out of the window, and forces her eyes open against the wind-borne dust.
A row of crooked rooftops appears on the horizon. Several pillars of smoke disperse in the air, covering the huts below in a smoky fog.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: These crooked roofs, and this smell of cooking... that's the town I remember!

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Maybe the Catastrophe Messengers were wrong.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It must be! Maybe it took a turn along the way and went somewhere else!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Look, Potlid, my home—

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Whatcha doing, Potlid?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Seventeen.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Eighteen.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Nineteen...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I'm counting the Originium pillars on the side of the road.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I see a lot more Originium clusters and cracks in the ground here than in other areas...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Didn't Alanna say there used to be a mine here? That would explain it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Just stop in front of those houses, Charlie.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Sure. Gotta fill up the water tank anyway.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: This is the place, Potlid. There used to a lady here who made two-color cake on the edge of town... what was her name again?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: She had a garden she took good care of, where she grew flowers she bought from distant markets.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But this doesn't look like a garden.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, sure doesn't...

steps.name: Barrenlands Settler
steps.text: Hey, don't step on my buds!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: A-Aunt Susan?

steps.name: Barrenlands Settler
steps.text: Who ya callin' yer aunt?!

steps.name: Barrenlands Settler
steps.text: Just stop moving! You've already stomped on three of my beets!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I-I'm sorry! I thought you were someone else.

steps.name: Barrenlands Settler
steps.text: You know how hard it is to find an unpolluted piece of farmland in this hellhole? You'd better pay up, outsider!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Outsider...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What's going on here?

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: The hose's connected, but it's gonna take a whole hour to fill... That's one huge water tank you've got there.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Thanks. Here, have a pack of smokes.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Didn't expect there to be an auto repair shop in this town. Guess this place is pretty well-connected.

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: Connected my arse. Can't buy a toothpick out here. Everything's gotta be brought in by car, so of course we take good care of 'em.

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: I only came here 'cause I was sick of being a mechanic. How was I supposed to know I'd be stuck back at my old job?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: You moved here? So you're not from this town?

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: Can you really call this dump a 'town'? You couldn't find dirt if you dug six feet under. It's all broken bricks and rotten wood.

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: No one would be here if the higher-ups weren't promising a big subsidy for some stupid 'environmental improvement' project.

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: Look at all that Originium scrap under your feet. It's only been, what, ten, twenty years since the Catastrophe. It's barely livable.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: ...Did a Catastrophe really hit this place?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: None of the old houses are left?

steps.name: Barrenlands Mechanic
steps.text: Nothing but a bunch of scrap that couldn't be sold.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (On the way here, I thought I might find someone I knew, some kind of trace from my memory.)

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (The Originium crystal clusters, the cracks in the ground, and even the broken tiles under my feet... they tell me all I need to know.)

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (The Messengers were right. The Catastrophe came. My home... is gone.)

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Are you alright, Lanns?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh? Oh, yeah, I'm good.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: You've been staring at that hill.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Was your house on the other side?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah... never mind. Just being silly.
Alanna sighs and rubs her own face.
Then she shrugs and goes back to being her bright and sunny self.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What a shame. Here I thought I was gonna get a free house!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Wouldn't be much point though, without water or electricity. Might as well live in a truck.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's warm in the truck, but on Rhodes Island we have our own rooms.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: You will surely get a bigger, comfier house, Lanns... and then, can I move in with you?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Ha! Who else would cook for me?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: You're not that bad of a cook yourself—

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: The tank's full, Alanna. You alright?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: I asked around. They all say...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, I know. Thanks anyway.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: I'll ask a few more. Maybe somebody knows where your house was... You might find some kinda closure, even if it's just a single brick.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: How would they know anything when they're all new here?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Let's just head on back to Rustdreg. There's still time to grab a few drinks with some more of my old friends.
Alanna turns around, avoiding looking at the bare slope and everything behind it.
No one knows where her home is better than herself.
She had climbed that slope many times, and slid all the way back home over the smooth grass.
She would grin while her mother looked at all the mud on her with chagrin.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: I'll go warm up the engine. No rush. I'll be waiting inside.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Let's go, Potlid. It'll be dark soon.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Anything you wanna eat once we get back to Rustdreg? How about some old fashioned cream pasta?
Alanna takes a few steps, but then realizes Potlid is not following her.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Look Lanns, I've got a scar on my knee.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Didn't you get that when you left the dorms? Does it still hurt?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Not anymore. It hurt a lot at first, but I didn't want to cry because there were a lot of people in the corridor. At that time, you said—

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: 'It's tiring trying to hold back tears. You're already hurting—don't tire yourself out too.'

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Then I cried, and after that it didn't hurt so much anymore.
Warmy approaches Alanna and takes her hand.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Your fingers have been trembling...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Now Warmy's holding your hand. There's no need to hold back.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's okay to feel scared or sad. I cried a lot when I first left home.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I started crying less after you started taking care of me.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But I won't be a little kid forever. I've grown up, and I can take care of you too.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I don't want you to be too hard on yourself. I know it's really tough, really tiring...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But it's not fair for me to weigh you down with all my emotional baggage... Potlid, you don't need to share my burden.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Isn't that what family's for? We share our burdens together, eat our meals together, and rub medicine on our wounds together.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: We've come such a long way together, Lanns. Aren't we family by now?
Alanna holds the small and warm hand in her own.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Yeah, we are.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: If you want to take another look, let's go. I'll be with you.
Lanns.
Mm?
The slope's so gentle, and the sand is so soft.
Mm-hm...
You've walked this path home so many times, haven't you?
Will you tell me? What this place used to look like...
I remember...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...I remember this place used to be covered in grass, and you'd slip after it rained if you weren't careful.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: There's still grass. But it's tiny, like it's just poking out of the soil.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Have you ever slid down a patch of grass?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: No. That sounds dangerous...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But fun too!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: When I was your age, I used to come here and slide down from the top of the slope.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Were you always so brave?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: More bored than brave.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I didn't make any new friends for a long time after moving here with my parents. But I didn't want to stay home all the time either, because it was always noisy at home...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Aren't homes supposed to be noisy? It sounds lively.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Um... not that kind of noisy. My mum and dad worked in the mines, where you'd have to shout to get heard over all the mine noises.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But they'd still do that at home, like they were yelling at each other. Always with a smile on their face, though. Even when they weren't yelling, they were always playing music at max volume.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And even when they did argue, they'd keep right on smiling, so I wouldn't notice. But I did. Because who cries when they're smiling?

spans.text: argue, they'd keep right on smiling, so I wouldn't notice. But I did. Because who cries when they're smiling?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So whenever they'd argue, I'd come here, slide down the grass, then climb back up and do it again.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: You were hurting inside, weren't you?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, and in the end I always had to go back home with mud all over my clothes. I made sure to put on a smile before I went in, so my mum wouldn't worry about me.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Later, they had an argument over that, too. After that one, pops made a bunch of stuff in the yard. A swing, a trampoline, even a little pavilion.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: My dad said he'd make me a swing and put it on the porch.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Why do grown-ups always think kids will like that kind of stuff?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I did. I love swings, trampolines, and pavilions... but my dad never got around to making it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Then I'll make 'em for you when we get back to Rhodes Island, fill up your room with them. How's that?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hehe...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: We're almost at the top. Soon we'll see the other side...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Why do you stop, Lanns?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: If you're too scared to look, close your eyes, and I'll look for you...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: How about that?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright.
Broken bricks, tiles, and charred wood creak as they walk across them.
In the gaps, tiny pieces of broken glass and Originium crystals reflect the last rays of sunset.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Is it just me, or have we been spending a long time walking these last few steps?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: We're almost there. Watch your step... take it easy.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: There's a lot of broken glass here. It's all twinkly. Like stars!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's all over the path! It's like...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Like what?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Like the stars are welcoming you home!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Home...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: If there's nothing there, don't tell me, just take me back to the truck.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Alright?
Potlid lets go and runs up.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid?!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Where are you? Are we on top of the hill?
She frantically reaches out, eyes still closed, and eventually finds Warmy's hand. Warmy is sobbing.
Sobbing, then laughing. She shakes Alanna by the shoulders and shouts—

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Look!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns—
Alanna opens her eyes slowly.
At the foot of the hill, a short distance away, she sees an overgrown ruin, the roof, windows, and doors all broken and battered.
Countless days and nights have passed. The wind, sun, and rain have caused even the strongest beams to rot and break.
But a single swing stands before the ruins.
Ugly, rusted, yet tough, it swings gently in the night breeze.
Creak—
'No! Look how high she's swinging, standing on the swing! She's going above the clothesline poles!'
'It's dangerous... bring me those canvas pants of yours you never wear. I'll make her a safety belt.'
'Don't cry, honey, don't cry, let mummy see where you got hurt... Oh no! You scratched your knee!'
'I told you it wasn't safe! Look at the frame! It just snapped!'
'This is all my fault... Sorry, Alanna. It's daddy's fault.'
'Where are you going at this hour?'
'Sleep now, honey. The sun's not up; it's just your daddy's soldering iron.'
'God knows what he's doing... Don't worry, I'll tell him you're not mad at him. You're such a good girl, Alanna.'
'Look, Alanna! Daddy made the swing stronger for you. Look at these steel pipes. See how thick they—What? You think it's ugly?'
'But it's so solid. I promise you, you won't fall no matter how high you swing—No, I take that back. Don't swing too high!'
'Daddy's fine. Gotta go to work. Let's play with the new swing once your mum and I get back tonight, alright?'
'Don't play it on your own, okay? Wait for mummy to come back and put the safety belt on you.'
'See you later, Alanna!'

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: They said there was an accident in the mine. I didn't even know what that meant at the time.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: All I remember is the carrot juice in the cup on the table, sloshing back and forth.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: A lot of people came by later. They wanted to take me away from home. They pointed at the strange clouds in the sky, said that the accident caused an Originium dust leak. A Catastrophe was coming, and I had to leave.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: They bashed open the door and took me away.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I... never had the chance to say goodbye to my home.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Some things don't feel so heavy once you've said them out loud.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But if you leave them in your heart, they become huge rocks. You always hated dragging rocks around when you were using the passenger compartment to haul cargo, didn't you?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, it's slow and you have to worry the whole way.
Alanna picks up a rock and throws it into the distance.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But now that I've thrown my rocks away, I can run free again!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You took me up this hill, Potlid. Now it's my turn to take you forward.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Huh? Lanns—
Alanna grins and pulls Warmy along towards the ruin at the foot of the hill.
She has walked this path home countless times. Now she recreates it, long after Catastrophe wiped it away.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: S-Slow down, Lanns!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Welcome to my place! Listen, they're all welcoming you—
Creak—
The night breeze blows through the cracks of the steel bars and chains. The sound of grinding metal echoes in the wind.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Wanna try it out? Don't worry, it's really solid.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: C-Can I really?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You always wanted a swing, didn't you? Here's one.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I'll make a better one for you once we get back to Rhodes Island!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But your dad made it for you...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I already played with it when I was little. It's your turn now. Every kid loves a swing!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I'm not a kid anymore!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That's right. You're all grown up, a big girl who's ready to share my burdens.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Once you're even taller than me, it'll be your turn to push me on the swing. But for now... let your Lanns take care of you a little longer.
Alanna lifts Warmy up onto the swing and grabs the safety belt.
The cloth on the surface is completely faded, but the metal chains within remain strong.
Warmy looks up and takes in Alanna's every little action as she fastens the safety belt.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: My mum spent a lot of time sewing this belt. She never let pops touch it—said she didn't feel comfortable if she didn't do it herself.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: She must have wanted to spend more time with you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: How does this thing work again? I think this was how she did it...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright! Totally secured. You won't fall no matter how high you swing.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The frame's really stable too. A little rusty, but it doesn't shake no matter how hard you swing.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I remember pops spent the whole night on it. The soldering iron cast a bright light on the window. Now that I look at the marks, I recognize them...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It's the most labor-intensive way of soldering, but also the strongest.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: There are a lot of things you don't realize until you grow up... That's what you always say to me when there's something you can't explain clearly.
Alanna begins pushing the swing gently. It carries Warmy along with a creaking that echoes through the quiet night.
Echoing into the distance.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns... I think it's starting to rain.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But the stars are still so bright...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: Shall we go?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, let's go. We'll talk later.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Say, Lanns, didn't you have a ticket?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Oh yeah! I almost forgot! What was up with that? Let me see...

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: I've been meaning to ask since you first brought it up, because I've never heard of no 'Residential Management Council'.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'The aforementioned building will be demolished if you do not pay the fine before the deadline.'

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It doesn't say where you pay it though. What's on the back?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'Your personal bank account will also be frozen. In order to avoid any interruption with your funds...'

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'Please transfer all funds in your account to our designated safe account. The account is managed by the Rim Billiton General Bank and your money will be absolutely safe.'

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It's a bloody scam!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Should've read the whole thing first. Guess my brain just turned off when I read it was gonna get torn down.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But we wouldn't be here if not for this scam letter.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Fate works in funny ways, huh?

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: The mechanic I talked to said that more people will move in once the environmental improvement project is complete. They'll build a new community here.

steps.name: Charlie the Sproglet
steps.text: The place where your home used to be will get turned into a playground with seesaws and slides. A place for kids with too much energy and nowhere to spent it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Doesn't sound so bad. What do you think, Potlid?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Yawns) Mm...
Alanna takes her gaze off the night outside the window and gazes upon Warmy's face as the young girl dozes off in her arms.
There is a tiny tear upon Warmy's eyelashes.
Alanna closes her own eyes too, and sees in her head that tiny trail full of starlight, and the swing waiting at its end.
'Goodbye,' she says in her mind.
Goodbye.
